newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index plunges on talk, poor result.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index plunges on talk, poor result.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share market closed sharply lower on Thursday amid widespread talk among analysts of a looming market clampdown.

Uncertainty in the midst of the company reporting season, exacerbated by Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co Ltd's announcement of a 30 percent slump in 1996 profits, also weighed on the recently-rangebound index.
No B share ended the day higher. The index lost 5.52 points or 3.29 percent to 162.14 points on thin turnover of HK$104.2 million compared with Wednesday's 109.7 million.
"We have heard a lot about a new clampdown on securities trading, which it is said will be announced by Beijing this weekend," a trader said.
"A lot of rumours are circulating in the market about a Beijing announcement in the next few days," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
Great Ocean's announcement of poor annual results also helped drag the B index down, analysts said.
The company said on Thursday its 1996 net profit slumped 30 percent from the 1995 figure to 35.6 million yuan because of stiff competition.
"There are not many B share companies," Xu Yinhui, analyst at China Guotai Securities, said. "If one posts poor results, investors get pessimistic about the rest."
Only two out of the 43 B share companies listed in Shenzhen have made their annual result public so far, with the official deadline on April 30 approaching.
Analysts said they did not expect the index to fall further.
"I think the index has fallen enough," the J&A trader said.
Great Ocean was the biggest loser, diving HK$0.33 or 7.62 percent to close at HK$4.00 on turnover of 1.53 million shares.
The A share index fell 9.96 points or 2.3 percent to end at 418.80 points on turnover of 9.6 billion yuan, compared with 10.3 billion yuan on Wednesday.
Computer hardware and software maker Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Co Ltd was the worst performer among the A shares, losing 2.77 yuan to 30.91 yuan as 3.4 million shares changed hands.
